Topics include search algorithms, logic, planning, machine learning, and applications from areas such as computer vision, robotics, and natural language processing. Consider this worked case: Students will explore how AI algorithms power real-world systems like recommendation engines and autonomous navigation. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.

Students cannot take and receive credit for this course if they have taken CSCI-630. beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how NIST AI Risk Management Framework operates in a concrete sequence. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Consider this worked case: Govern establishes policies, Map documents context and impacts, Measure analyzes risks, and Manage prioritizes responses. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Consider this worked case: In a healthcare AI system, data quality and fairness are critical to ensure accurate diagnoses and equitable outcomes. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Monitoring continues after deployment because context and system behavior can change. Consider this worked case: A self-driving car's AI must continuously monitor road conditions and sensor data to adapt to new environments. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Machine Learning Workflow Overview, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Consider this worked case: Developing a spam filter involves cleaning email data, training a classifier, validating on unseen data, and testing performance. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Supervised and Unsupervised Methods with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Consider this worked case: Supervised learning trains a model to classify images as cats or dogs, whereas unsupervised learning groups similar images by color patterns. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.

beats.narration: Use Preprocessing and Leakage Prevention to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Consider this worked case: Scaling features using only training data statistics prevents test data information from influencing the model's performance. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.

beats.narration: Connect Pipelines and Cross-Validation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined data splits. Consider this worked case: A single pipeline ensures that image resizing and normalization are applied identically during training and testing, while cross-validation evaluates model stability across multiple data folds. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.

beats.narration: Finish with Evaluation Metrics and Hyperparameter Selection as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Consider this worked case: For medical diagnosis, precision and recall are prioritized over accuracy, and hyperparameters are tuned only on validation data before final testing. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.

sources.author: scikit-learn developers
sources.excerpt: Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Unsupervised methods identify structure without target labels. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Pipelines combine preprocessing and estimators so the same transformations are applied consistently. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined data splits. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Hyperparameter selection must remain separate from final test evaluation. Leakage, distribution shift, overfitting, and unexamined assumptions can invalidate results.

sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.excerpt: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Govern establishes policies, responsibilities, and accountability for AI risk. Map documents context, intended use, affected people, and potential impacts. Measure uses qualitative and quantitative methods to analyze identified risks. Manage prioritizes risks and allocates resources for response and monitoring. Risk analysis considers data quality and uncertainty. It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness. Monitoring continues after deployment because context and system behavior can change.
